plain_description.what: No calls. For each benchmark in the combined dataset, the test measured the share of its held-out questions that land in a cell dominated by a different benchmark. It compared the tree built without topic labels but separately within each source benchmark (source-conditioned, not label-free) with per-source k-means clustering.
plain_description.why: It asks whether the tree mixes benchmarks more than plain k-means does, which would make it a worse index for checking coverage.
plain_description.information: If the tree mixed more, it would be the worse tool for coverage audits. Equivalence means neither is worse on this measure. Result: done. The two are equivalent within a 2-point margin (about 3% of items land in a foreign-dominated cell under both). This is equivalence within a margin, not 'no difference'. It is not a claim that foreign filing is an error, and it does not compare how well the two separate benchmarks.
